subject: HelioHealth: post-call vendor comparison & PoC test plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Dawson <emma@heliohealth.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: HelioHealth: post-call vendor comparison & PoC test plan

Thanks again for your time this morning — appreciated the candid discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same playbook.

Key pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable inference cost at peak loads (esp. nightly batch/reporting).
- Production latency spikes causing downstream UI timeouts for clinicians.
- Data governance: need audit logs and optional VPC isolation for PHI.

Stated goals:
- Latency: 99th percentile < 200ms for common chat flows (50–150 tokens).
- Cost: reduce per-token inference spend relative to current provider by ~35% over 6 months.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence and IP isolation for patient data.

Competitive landscape notes from our call:
- You are demoing three vendors this week (current incumbent + Vendor X). Your evaluation will prioritize latency consistency and cost per 10k tokens.

Proposed PoC scope and tests (high-level):
1) Traffic mix replay (production traces) — 72 hour run to validate batching behavior and tail latency.
2) Edge-case prompt tests — hallucination/regression checks using the 150-test prompt set you shared.
3) Cost projection run — simulated 30-day traffic to validate our cost profile with recommended batching/quantization.

Deliverables we will provide by EOD Tue:
- A filled bakeoff matrix (attached: helio-bakeoff-matrix-v1.xlsx) comparing latency, throughput, features (VPC/KMS/SLA).
- A test harness and scripts (poctest-scripts.zip) and instructions for running in your environment.
- A short runbook for the PoC with suggested SLAs and rollback criteria.

Open / action items for HelioHealth:
- Confirm which production traces (dates/time windows) you want us to replay.
- Internal priority: which metric is tie-breaker — latency or cost? (we recommended latency for clinician UX).
- Share contact for Legal/Procurement so we can pre-send an NDA/POC MSA draft.

Next meeting: propose a 30-minute sync on Thu to go over the matrix and lock the PoC start date.

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: helio-bakeoff-matrix-v1.xlsx, poctest-scripts.zip, redwood-quickstart.pdf

From: Emma Dawson <emma@heliohealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@heliohealth.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T14:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelioHealth: post-call vendor comparison & PoC test plan

Thanks Vanessa — super clear and helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Priority: UX latency should be the primary tie-breaker; cost is important but we will accept slightly higher baseline cost if 99p is consistent.
2) Traces: we will share three representative windows from July (weekday peak, nightly batch, and weekend low). Rajiv will upload to the shared Drive link you included.
3) Procurement: Alex is the procurement lead — he will review your POC MSA draft. Our procurement timeline aims to finalize a vendor by Oct 8.

One ask: can Redwood include a short test that exercises key failure modes (GPU OOM / transient node loss) so we can see graceful degradation and fallbacks? That was the incumbent's weak spot.

We'll block Thu 11:00–11:30 PT for the sync; thanks for moving fast.

—
Emma Dawson
Head of Product, HelioHealth
emma@heliohealth.com | +1 (206) 555-0124

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Dawson <emma@heliohealth.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@heliohealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelioHealth: post-call vendor comparison & PoC test plan

Great — thanks Emma. We will add a failure-mode test that simulates node preemption and GPU OOM to show our graceful fallbacks and model variant routing. Specifics we will include in the test harness:
- 99p latency target: 200ms (chat flows), 95p target: 120ms (for standard prompts).
- Batching/queueing behavior: histogram and per-request trace export.
- Fallback rules: automatic model-variant routing + region failover (we'll show logs).
- Cost projection: baseline and worst-case scenarios with our recommended caching/batch settings.

Internal ask (cc Marissa + Rishi):
- Marissa: run the PoC harness on a 72-hour replay using the July traces Emma will share; collect latency distribution, token-level cost, and failure-mode outcomes.
- Rishi: prepare the quantization/infra recommendation for the PoC (target quantized variants we plan to surface for Helio).
- I'll draft the POC MSA and share to Alex; legal points to preempt: data residency, access logs retention, and SLA credits.

I'll attach the test-run playbook to the Drive folder and send a short runbook to Alex after this thread.

—
Vanessa
